slides.0.subtitle: History, geography, varieties and classification
slides.1.title: Level 1 key points
slides.1.highlights.0.title: History
slides.1.highlights.0.content: An old wine culture → the 1784 decree and the Heuriger → 1872 phylloxera → the 1985 glycol scandal and strict law → a turn to dry quality wines → the first DAC in 2002
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Geography and climate
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Concentrated in the east at 47–48° N; continental-Pannonian climate; the influence of the Danube and Neusiedler See
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Varieties
slides.1.highlights.2.content: White: Grüner Veltliner (about one third), Riesling, Welschriesling; red: Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch, St. Laurent
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Classification
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Wein → Landwein → Qualitätswein (including Kabinett) → Prädikat (from Spätlese); DACs are defined by regional style
slides.1.content: Figures that differ between sources (number of DACs, area by state, the Ausbruch minimum) are not examined; go by the year and official sources.

In Austria, which level is NOT a Prädikatswein?
Kabinett belongs to Qualitätswein; Prädikat starts at Spätlese.
